title: Sourced Group acquires Open House estate agents
summary:
Sourced Group has acquired Open House Estate Agents, bringing 104 franchisees into its network and offering them access to a funded acquisitions programme. The combined network now comprises more than 230 franchisees across the UK.

The post Sourced Group acquires Open House estate agents appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Public support for local housebuilding outweighs opposition
summary:
More than two in five British adults support new homes being built within three miles of their residence, according to research from Barclays. The findings suggest that 'YIMBY' sentiment is more prevalent than 'NIMBY' attitudes across the UK, with support strongest among younger generations.

The post Public support for local housebuilding outweighs opposition appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Housing minister confirms ‘acute’ UK housing crisis
summary:
Housing Minister Matthew Pennycook has described Britain's housing situation as an "acute and entrenched crisis", signalling the government's intention to expand council house construction significantly. The minister highlighted that 64,000 new council homes were delivered last year, the highest annual rate since 2014-2015.

The post Housing minister confirms ‘acute’ UK housing crisis appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: LRG acquires 200-year-old Henry Adams estate agency
summary:
LRG is set to expand its footprint across southern England through the acquisition of Henry Adams, a property agency with origins dating back to 1826. The deal, expected to complete on 1st September, will add 12 branches across Sussex, Surrey and Hampshire to LRG's portfolio.

The post LRG acquires 200-year-old Henry Adams estate agency appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Edinburgh council to vote on 300% second home tax premium
summary:
Edinburgh City Council will vote tomorrow on whether to implement a 300% council tax premium on second homes. The decision could see affected property owners in Band H facing annual bills of approximately £16,000.

The post Edinburgh council to vote on 300% second home tax premium appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Tax concerns outweigh regulation fears for UK landlords
summary:
Taxation has emerged as the primary concern for UK landlords, surpassing worries about increased regulation, according to new research. The analysis found that 62.7% of landlords intend to maintain their current portfolio over the next year, while only 3.9% plan to expand their holdings.

The post Tax concerns outweigh regulation fears for UK landlords appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Harlow site acquisition backed by £1.8m bridging finance
summary:
Recognise Bank has provided a £1.836 million bridging loan to facilitate the acquisition of a mixed-use commercial property in Harlow, Essex. The 18-month facility was structured at 57% LTV to enable a civil engineering firm to complete the purchase within several weeks.

The post Harlow site acquisition backed by £1.8m bridging finance appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Prime London property values down 25% as tax changes bite
summary:
Prime Central London property values have fallen by up to 25% in some cases as tax changes targeting non-domiciled residents impact the upper end of the market. Properties above £15 million have been particularly affected, with international buyers historically accounting for around 70% of transactions in this segment.

The post Prime London property values down 25% as tax changes bite appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Newcastle leads rental yields at 6.9%, national average hits 5.9%
summary:
Newcastle upon Tyne has emerged as the highest-yielding rental market in England, with average yields reaching 6.9%, according to new research from The Letting Partnership. The analysis calculated the national average rental yield at 5.9%, derived from an average house price of £293,262 and monthly rent of £1,446.

The post Newcastle leads rental yields at 6.9%, national average hits 5.9% appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Student landlords face Ground 4A possession deadline
summary:
The upcoming academic year marks the first test of new possession rules for student landlords following changes introduced under the Renters' Rights Act. Landlords who missed transitional deadlines are unlikely to obtain possession under Ground 4A during the remaining 2026 window.

The post Student landlords face Ground 4A possession deadline appeared first on PropertyWire.
